card.title: Name What It Cost
card.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the emotional cost of what happened, not merely the event itself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You apologised for missing my concert. What do you think the empty seat felt like?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know the timetable. I'm asking about the seat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You felt let down. I watched the recording this morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you saw me look at the door before the encore. Can you understand how it felt to keep expecting you?

beats.speaker: A

mechanism: A asks B to recognize the experience of waiting through a performance rather than only explain absence.
confusable: Unlike seeking another apology for the event, A must direct attention to its emotional cost.
comparison: D75-a uses a recorded glance before the encore; D75-b uses repeated message drafting during silence.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
